newsitem.title: UK: EU grain exporters seek more world market buyers.
newsitem.headline: EU grain exporters seek more world market buyers.

text.p: European grain exporters are largely content with the rate of exports, but there are still some notable absentees from the world market early in 1997.
Egypt is one country they expect to see soon. But the delay is not creating too much concern. "It's not so bad. They'll be coming," one analyst at a big European trading house said.

Latest EU grain export commitments between July 1, 1996 and January 7, 1997 were 33 percent above their year-ago level, mostly the result of higher wheat and barley sales, member-country officials said.
Export commitments so far come to 16.986 million tonnes. The EU is hoping to export some 29 million tonnes of grain by the end of the marketing year.

The analyst also expected to see more demand from Iraq in the near future. Iraq has already scheduled a tender for 100,000 tonnes of French wheat for January 14, with delivery to follow in March and April. This deal would be under the UN oil-for-food deal.
The year started with rumours in the international market that Egypt was about to tender for possibly 500,000 tonnes of wheat.

International Grains Council analyst Bill De Maria put overall world market interest at around the same level as at the same stage in 1996, but noted that India and Iraq had helped bump up the totals.

India's state-run State Trading Corporation said on Wednesday that it had contracted to import 1.25 million ttonnes of wheat in 1996/97 (April-March) with the first shipments expected to arrive later this month.
As well, Pakistan is expected to open bids on Sunday in a tender for 312,000 tonnes of U.S. or Australian white wheat.
But De Maria did detect a element of reluctance on the part of potential buyers. "People are buying at a slow rhythm in the hope of falling prices," he said.

He saw price leadership in the world market passing from Argentina to Australia before long. On January 6 the Argentine government said exporters there had accumulated contracts to export 6.5 million tonnes of 1996/97 wheat, compared to sales of 3 million tonnes by the same time last year.
Much of the rest of Argentina's likely exports of approaching 10 million tonnes was likely to be heading for Brazil, De Maria said.

European exporters are also watching Russia and China for signs that they will start looking for grain on the world market, although China is seen as less likely to buy just yet after record harvests in 1996. --London newsroom, +44 171 542 7928
